Separates request and reply UDP endpoints (127.0.0.1:2000/2001), sharing stream1. Externalize endpoints/streams and allocate isolated ports; stream identity alone is not an application session.

Starts an embedded SHARED driver in a client-specific directory, connects Aeron to that directory, and owns the AgentRunner/barrier/client/driver lifecycle. Directory deletion and quietClose suit a throwaway demo; preserve durable directories and surface failures in a real owner.

Reuses header and response decoder flyweights, wrapping at callback offset and using received blockLength/version. It dispatches only by templateId and signals completion for any response: add schema/length/correlation checks and fragment assembly before treating a reply as an acknowledgement.

Models outbound connect, reply subscription readiness, request and result as explicit states; reuses a direct buffer and encoders. Its blocking readiness loops have no deadline, three-offer retry can silently lose a command while state advances, UUID/string correlation allocates, and doWork returns0 even on work. Retain exact pending bytes and poll incrementally with truthful work counts.

Uses a separate server driver directory and SHARED threading, then closes runner/Aeron/driver after the barrier. Take the ownership wiring, but add constructor-failure cleanup and propagate errors instead of printing and waiting indefinitely.

Reuses SBE flyweights and an expandable response buffer, reads variable fields in schema order, and dynamically opens a client reply publication. Opening a connection blocks inside the fragment callback; only one publication is stored, three failed offers can lose the result, String decoding/uppercase allocates, and no schema/bounds checks or FragmentAssembler are present. Use bounded per-client state only when its contract requires it.

Creates the request subscription in onStart and returns subscription.poll count, allowing AgentRunner to idle correctly. onClose explicitly closes only the adapter publication; close its subscription too when the agent owns it rather than relying on the surrounding Aeron close.

Console logging uses LOG_LEVEL defaultinfo and time/thread/message pattern; Logback debug=false. Per-message logging and argument boxing/formatting are not a zero-allocation or latency baseline; keep operational logs out of measured hot-path claims.

RPC schema688/version1 uses the standard8-byte little-endian header; templates10 connect,11 request,12 response. URI/parameters/result/correlation are sequential UTF-8 varData with uint32 length and max250; return stream is uint16. Respect field order, byte limits and the narrower stream range; these identities are unrelated to Spine schema100.

FIX SBE1.0 Draft XSD validates schema/type names, primitive types, presence/version/offset attributes and fixed-field then group then varData structure. The three assigned copies are byte-identical (SHA256 a3dcc0e332f1e8ba348c196454637c524aaef0d9b4d45dfdfe0fe63ff9b0fc44); read once and verify all copies. XSD validation does not validate runtime frame lengths, expected identity, application64KiB limits or logical semantics.

Single-consumer reads a OneToOneRingBuffer and signals at the target integer. It returns0 instead of ringBuffer.read count and checks only the terminal value, so it does not prove every input arrived; track count/order for acceptance tests.

Uses tryClaim, writes directly into ring storage, then commit: no separate per-message payload buffer. It starts at1 and increments before write, so first value is2 and the final iteration can write sendCount+1; correct boundaries before using it as a count benchmark, report work, and abort a successful claim if encoding fails.

Allocates one direct buffer of16384 bytes plus RingBufferDescriptor.TRAILER_LENGTH, one SPSC ring, and separate busy-spin sender/receiver runners. Topology must remain exactly one producer/one consumer; busy spinning consumes dedicated CPU and the terminal-value barrier is not a full delivery or allocation measurement.

Each receiver has its own BroadcastReceiver and CopyBroadcastReceiver over shared storage. Copying provides a stable callback view and detects lapping; broadcast is not backpressured reliable delivery. Return receive count rather than0 and keep the callback borrowed.

Reuses an ExpandableArrayBuffer and transmits typed4-byte integers through BroadcastTransmitter. The barrier signals after transmission, not after both consumers have applied the final message; count acks independently if final delivery matters. Expansion/logging and method-reference adaptation prevent a blanket zero-allocation claim.

Allocates65536 bytes plus broadcast trailer, one transmitter and two independent receivers. A sleeping sender intentionally avoids lapping that busy spin can expose. Use broadcast for lossy latest/control distribution with a recovery mechanism, not as Spine canonical history.

Single reader of a ManyToOneRingBuffer signals on one terminal integer. Return the read count and validate per-producer identities/counts; arrival of sender1 terminal value does not show sender2 completed.

MPSC claim/write/commit pattern reuses ring memory; same increment-before-write boundary as the SPSC example emits2 first and may emit sendCount+1. Keep producer state unchanged on insufficient capacity and report actual work.

Source initializes currentCountItem=sendCount*2, then immediately returns whenever currentCountItem>sendCount, so this pinned sample never publishes from sender2. Fix that condition and prove both producers contribute before treating StartHere as an MPSC workload.

Creates one preallocated MPSC ring with two sender runners and one receiver, all busy spinning. Agent construction illustrates topology/lifecycle, but the sender2 condition and terminal-only barrier mean the exact sample does not establish two-producer correctness or throughput.

Shows getAndAddLong, getAndSetLong and compareAndSetLong on an8-byte direct UnsafeBuffer. It is a single-thread semantic test, not concurrency proof; preserve alignment and select acquire/release/volatile semantics for actual communication.

Three failed offers can lose events while timers are removed; use a pending output before advancing state, truthful work counts and bounded nonblocking readiness. O(n) scans, per-timer allocation and mutable wall-clock deadlines are demo choices.

Cancel and fire responses can both occur, so define application terminal-state/idempotency semantics. Fixed three-offer attempts can silently lose commands, readiness blocks without deadline, and subscriptions lack fragment assembly/schema/bounds checks.

Generates a separate local admin schema and depends on the shared Cluster protocol; adds JLine/picocli and builds the correct admin uber JAR. application.mainClass names io.aeron.samples.admin.Admin rather than the actual com.aeroncookbook.rfq.admin.Admin; validate task/manifest launch paths independently.

Documents commands, gateway-style local-SBE-to-Cluster-SBE conversion and environment variables. Its sample uses add-instrument instead of the actual instrument-add command and describes two users while code accepts three; check concrete CLI names and paths against source.
Launches the admin uber JAR with JDK internal-misc and zip opens. Those flags reflect its runtime dependencies; do not infer low allocation or production readiness from launch success.

Installs bash/wget and downloads aeron-all 1.47.0 diagnostic tooling without a checksum. That tool version differs from cookbook 1.52.1 and Spine 1.53.0; use a verified tool matching the deployment instead of this stale download.

Owns a JLine/picocli REPL and AgentRunner connected by an 8192-byte OneToOneRingBuffer backed by direct storage plus trailer. Startup auto-connect ignores a failed ring write; EOF exits without closing the runner, unlike explicit exit. Keep one producer/consumer and make cleanup/full-ring policy explicit.

Picocli root owns the command set and reader, sharing a single OneToOneRingBuffer producer with subcommands. Messages use type 10 and a failed write prints an error rather than retrying/persisting; ring capacity and single-producer ownership must remain explicit.

Encodes baseport, response port, cluster hosts and advertised local host into a reusable admin SBE buffer. Connection configuration is supplied via CLI/environment; bound strings and validate endpoint/port values before publishing.
Encodes a header-only local disconnect command for the transport agent. This illustrates control/data commands on the same owned ring; disconnect is not a durable admission cancellation.

Reuses AddInstrument encoder/header/buffer to queue CUSIP, enabled flag and minimum size. Boolean.parseBoolean maps unknown text to false, and defaults permit empty CUSIP; validate user input instead of relying on a generated fixed-width string setter.
Queues SetInstrumentEnabledFlag with FALSE using a reused encoder. Shares one wire template with enable; require a valid identifier and distinguish local queue acceptance from Cluster confirmation.
Queues SetInstrumentEnabledFlag with TRUE using a reused encoder. This is command construction only; the domain confirms whether the CUSIP exists.
Queues a header-only ListInstrumentsCommand; its CUSIP option is unused. Listing demonstrates a repeating-group response rather than a query-specific filtered projection.

Queues RFQ ID and accepting user. The admin schema also declares rfqQuoteId but the CLI does not populate it and the bridge ignores it; remove/define unused required fields instead of relying on initial buffer contents.

Queues RFQ ID and canceling user, defaulting RFQ ID to Integer.MIN_VALUE. Required identifiers should be validated before queueing; caller-supplied user IDs alone do not prove requester authorization.
Queues RFQ ID, countering user and integer price. Reused codec/buffer construction is useful; correct alternating-party checks and business price semantics are not supplied by this command.

Queues RFQ creation with CLI quantity/user/CUSIP and an absolute local-wall-clock expiry 30 seconds ahead. Non-buy input silently becomes SELL; declare epoch/time units, validate side and account for clock skew before the Cluster compares expiry to logged time.

Queues RFQ ID, quoting user and integer price into the admin protocol. Integer price is an opaque demo amount without declared financial scaling; existence/authorization/turn validation belongs in the service.

Queues RFQ ID and rejecting user through the admin RejectRfqCommand. The schema’s price field is not populated by this CLI nor by its translation path; fully initialize required fields in any production protocol.

Template switch reuses decoders to display confirmations/broadcasts and clear PendingMessageManager entries by correlation; session/leader callbacks display transport events. Minimum header check is not full decoding validation, String/ANSI logging allocates, and malformed/stale broadcast correlations must not acknowledge unrelated requests.

Owns AeronCluster/MediaDriver, polls CLI commands and egress, sends 250 ms keepalives and translates admin SBE into Cluster SBE with new correlation UUID Strings. It always returns0 despite work, allows ten offer attempts, tracks commands even when offers fail, and does not retain durable bytes or deduplicate retries; repeated connect can replace resources without closing them.
CONNECTED/NOT_CONNECTED enum is only the admin’s local connection flag. It is not quorum health, committed-head agreement, recorded-head freshness or an indication that a submission was applied.

Builds styled terminal text and redraws an active prompt while asynchronous egress arrives. Useful UI integration, but formatting and terminal I/O allocate/block and are not a trading/research hot-path pattern.
Record carries absolute timeout, correlation String and message-type label. Its immutable shape helps diagnostics; it does not own the command bytes or persist admission progress.

LinkedList-backed queue tracks five-second wall-clock timeouts, removes by correlation and logs one overdue request per duty cycle. This is timeout notification only: no exact retry, reconnect persistence, bounded admission slots or server dedup; use monotonic time for local elapsed deadlines.

Environment then system-property/default helpers resolve hosts, response port and user ID, plus eth0 IPv4 lookup with localhost fallback. Validate ports/IDs and explicit advertised addresses; eth0 assumptions and silently swallowed lookup failures are deployment conveniences.

Vendored FIX SBE XSD identical to the Cluster-protocol copy; validates XML structure, groups and schema evolution attributes. It does not enforce runtime endpoint, identity, command-body or allocation limits.

Local CLI-to-agent schema also uses ID101/version1 but different layouts/template assignments than the Cluster schema: no correlation fields, int32 quantity and varData connection hosts. Translate explicitly and keep channels/modules separated; identical schema IDs do not make these formats interchangeable.

Builds admin and Cluster images from sibling directories with --no-cache. Assumes a particular working directory and prebuilt JARs, lacks fail-fast handling and does not build Java itself; do not execute as a safe deployment transaction.

Separate java-library generates the shared Cluster schema with XSD validation and compileJava dependency. Generated source is a build artifact, not checked-in handwritten logic; keep Spine’s SBE 1.38.1 pin when borrowing this task shape.
Explains generated-code module/task separation, but mentions auction terminology and an incorrect src/java/main path. The actual schema lives at src/main/resources/protocol/protocol-codecs.xml.

Vendored FIX SBE XML-schema validation boilerplate, byte-identical to the admin XSD. Governs field/group/data ordering, primitive/composite types and evolution attributes; not a runtime binary validator or an application-specific protocol.

Cluster schema 101/version 1 declares instrument records/commands, RFQ commands, confirmations, broadcasts and repeating InstrumentsList. Uses fixed nine-byte CUSIP, 36-byte correlation Strings and millisecond expiry; inspect every encoder for required-field initialization and enforce lengths/schema/version on ingress.

Builds a Java 21 root-owned Cluster image and includes entrypoint plus diagnostic/snapshot scripts. No persistent volume or image-digest/security policy is defined here; operational commands need explicit paths and matching tool versions.

Selects the first /dev/shm directory containing aeron and runs AeronStat watch=false. Explicitly select the owned driver directory and matching JAR when multiple instances coexist; do not parse arbitrary first-match counters as authority.

Service application depends on shared generated Cluster protocol, Agrona, Aeron samples and logging; runSingleNodeCluster and uberJar name ClusterApp. Use minimal exact runtime dependencies in Spine, not the sample umbrella module or this version catalog.

Selects a first matching Cluster directory then runs ClusterTool errors. Useful diagnostic tool shape, but shell directory inference and its old downloaded tool version need replacement with explicit pinned paths.
Runs ClusterTool describe on an inferred Cluster path to inspect mark-file metadata. Descriptors aid diagnosis; they are not a committed canonical-output fence.

Forwards JVM arguments, prefers IPv4 and sets Aeron IPC MTU 8 KiB before launching ClusterApp. This is an IPC framing choice, not a network-MTU guarantee; maximum payload/fragmentation rules still apply.
Runs ErrorStat against an inferred MediaDriver directory. Use driver/Archive/Cluster error reports to explain failures, but bind the correct directory rather than an arbitrary first match.
Runs LossStat for the inferred driver directory. Loss observation is transport telemetry; a quiet loss report does not prove every application event was recorded/applied.

Parses three separate AeronStat snapshots and hardcodes role 2/election 17/module 1 as LEADER. Counters can change between reads and enum codes vary; quote/check shell values and prefer typed pinned counters or ClusterTool is-leader.

Lists local launch, Cluster environment variables and bundled operations scripts. Some names are stale (streamsstat versus streamstat); treat executable script filenames and pinned tool APIs as authority.

Installs shell/procps/less/sysstat/wget and downloads aeron-all 1.47.0. Reconcile diagnostic binaries with the actual Cluster version; downloads/apt state are not reproducible or checksum-verified in this demo.

Requests ClusterTool snapshot on an inferred Cluster directory. This mutates Cluster state and needs authorized operations; in this RFQ example the application snapshot callback is unimplemented, so a tool request does not prove restorable domain state.

Environment/system-property bootstrap creates ClusterConfig from node index, host list and port base, sets UDP ingress and a three-second leader heartbeat, then owns driver/Archive/consensus/container lifecycles. DNS retry/delay is deployment startup scaffolding; validate addresses/node bounds and replace container-local data paths for persistence.

Instrument object keeps immutable CUSIP/minimum size and mutable enabled state; equality/hash use CUSIP identity. This is a simple service-thread domain value, not a validated financial instrument definition or immutable snapshot.

INTERACTIVE versus SNAPSHOT_LOAD indicates whether instrument insertion should reply to a user. Suppressing side effects during restoration is useful, but neither enum value supplies schema validation or a complete snapshot implementation.

Agrona Object2ObjectHashMap stores CUSIP instruments; insertion and enabled changes produce confirmations, listing materializes values with stream().toList(). Duplicate inserts overwrite, size is unbounded and hash iteration is not stable wire order; validate identifiers/limits and sort if deterministic encoded lists matter.
Explicitly states the RFQ workflow is unrealistic and exists to demonstrate a stateful multi-user Cluster application. Keep this limitation attached to any extracted state-machine/business pattern.

Mutable RFQ aggregate keeps immutable creation attributes, participant/price fields and singleton state objects; methods guard transitions. The initial lastCounterUser sentinel is Integer.MIN_VALUE, which must match downstream comparisons; no accepted/rejected user getters exist for the event fields the schema declares.

Deterministic command handlers validate users/instruments, assign IDs, mutate RFQs, confirm/broadcast and schedule expiry. Demo list stream searches/closures/logs allocate; int lastCounterUser is compared to Long.MIN_VALUE so checks never match, some turn checks are inverted, and rejectRfq lacks return after emitting a rejection. Correlation strings do not deduplicate command retries.
Terminal singleton rejects every transition and returns null. It does not implement the ACCEPTED-to-COMPLETED edge in the diagram; do not assume a trade-completion workflow exists.
Terminal canceled singleton rejects transitions and allocates nothing per access. Persist the explicit state ID and test that cancellation prevents later timer-driven mutation.
Inconsistent singleton reports EXPIRED and QUOTED as permitted but transitionTo always returns null. Treat this as an unfinished demo state; never copy its contract into a completed-trade reducer.
Stateless singleton supports repeated counters and acceptance/cancel/rejection/expiry. The state alone does not determine which participant may respond, so audit the Rfqs turn checks separately.

Stateless singleton permits expiry, quote and cancel and selects the corresponding singleton. Its executable transitions do not include the CREATED-to-REJECTED edge shown in the accompanying PlantUML diagram.
Terminal expired singleton rejects transitions. It demonstrates timer-driven terminal state, but the application must restore pending timer/model identity for recovery.
Stateless singleton permits acceptance, counter, expiry, cancel and rejection. Reusable transition table pattern; party/turn authorization remains the aggregate/application handler’s responsibility.
Terminal rejected singleton rejects transitions. The state object is simple; handler validation must return before mutation after a rejected command.
State interface exposes explicit state ID, permitted-target check and transition result. A production transition contract should guarantee a nonnull next state whenever canTransitionTo returns true.
Static Agrona Int2ObjectHashMap resolves IDs to stateless singleton state implementations. Avoid per-transition allocation; callers must reject unknown IDs instead of accepting null as a model state.

Stable explicit short IDs enumerate CREATED=0, QUOTED=1, COUNTERED=2, ACCEPTED=3, REJECTED=4, EXPIRED=5, CANCELED=6, COMPLETED=7. Never persist enum ordinal implicitly; fromId currently returns null on unknown IDs rather than rejecting malformed state.

PlantUML documents the intended RFQ lifecycle, including CREATED-to-REJECTED and ACCEPTED-to-COMPLETED edges absent from executable states. Use it to design transition acceptance tests, not as proof of implemented behavior.

Agrona IntHashSet contains hardcoded user IDs 500, 501, 502 for membership checks. It illustrates primitive-key membership, not authentication, session-to-user binding, entitlement checks or a replicated user-management workflow.

Composition root wires context, sessions, SBE adapter, instruments, users, RFQs and timers; command/timer callbacks use the logged Cluster timestamp. onStart explicitly does not load snapshots and onTakeSnapshot is unimplemented: do not prune the command log assuming application state was captured.

Optional open/close observer interface carries the ClientSession and Cluster-provided timestamp. This separates transport session notifications from the domain, but session existence is not authenticated user identity.

Tracks sessions in an insertion-ordered ArrayList plus Agrona Long2ObjectHashMap lookup, notifying an optional listener on open/close. Both are service-thread-owned, unbounded, and the mutable session list escapes; preserve ownership and explicit iteration order if simplifying containers.

Domain-facing interface separates instrument/RFQ confirmations and broadcasts from encoding and session offers. Use its separation when several transport-independent operations justify it; it is not an independent durable event stream.

Reuses per-template SBE encoders and one ExpandableDirectByteBuffer for confirmations, lists and broadcasts. Populate every required field on every wrap: several broadcasts write RFQ ID into user-ID fields, and accepted/rejected/quoted events omit schema fields including correlations/participants, exposing stale buffer contents.

Checks only minimum header length, then dispatches reused generated decoders into the instrument/RFQ model. Add schema/version/root/variable/group bounds validation; notably snapshot InstrumentRecord is also admitted through command dispatch, so snapshot restoration should have a distinct validated context.
Small domain context contract exposes logged Cluster time plus reply/broadcast operations. It makes deterministic model time available without having the model read a process wall clock.

Carries the current command session and logged timestamp, replying directly or broadcasting across tracked sessions with three offer attempts. Its retry-exhaustion path closes the current requester rather than the targetSession; null replay sessions, terminal CLOSED and dropped egress require explicit policy.

Scaffold for polling a snapshot Image to EOS and offering records with a retry limit. It writes no state, recognizes no record templates and never marks snapshotFullyLoaded; it also lacks fragment assembly and robust EOS/closed/callback-failure handling. Study lifecycle shape only.

Agrona Long2ObjectHashMap binds deterministic Cluster timer IDs to Runnable tasks; schedule retries use the Cluster idle strategy and expiry updates logged time before invoking a task. Restore does not advance its correlation counter and closures are not serialized; snapshot IDs/tasks, handle cancellation races and retain Cluster time units explicitly.
Message-only console appender with LOG_LEVEL default info makes domain activity visible. RFQ handlers, retry loops and lifecycle logging must be separated from low-allocation latency measurements.

Uses ps/grep/awk to find a Cluster PID then calls jstack. Bind an explicit process ID because broad grep can return several/unrelated processes; stack dumping is diagnosis rather than a latency-safe background poll.

Runs StreamStat against the inferred driver directory. Useful publisher/subscriber position diagnostics; physical stream positions require generation/session pinning before comparing logical progress.

Builds Java/images, deletes both sample namespaces and reapplies manifests for local Docker Desktop. Namespace deletion is destructive and the relative ./gradlew/module paths assume an older layout; review exact working directory and data ownership before running.

Wires three Cluster nodes and two interactive admins on fixed bridge IPs with 1 GiB shared memory and declared bridge MTU 9000. No persistent Archive/Cluster mounts, readiness checks or production isolation are supplied; Docker depends_on is not quorum readiness.

Executes noderole.sh in each known Compose node and selects output containing LEADER. Depends on interactive docker exec, fixed names and fragile role parsing; prefer version-matched ClusterTool is-leader exit status.

Explains building/starting Compose, connecting two admins and manually stopping a leader. Names engine containers that current YAML names node containers, and the procedure has no automated replay/receipt equivalence assertions.

408-frame 1470×868 terminal demonstration asset linked from README, decoded and inspected as an illustration. It is not an executable test, latency benchmark, recoverability proof or API specification.
Finds an admin then kubectl execs the opened-JDK admin JAR. Interactive operational convenience; quote/validate discovered pod and use an explicit namespace/session lifecycle.

Parses the first Name line from kubectl describe pod using grep/head and shell splitting. Prefer structured kubectl selectors/output because textual parsing is fragile with multiple pods or missing output.

Executes the hardcoded noderole.sh check in each StatefulSet pod and returns the first LEADER. Fixed membership/order and textual counter parsing do not supply a consistent, version-independent leadership authority.

Deletes the pod returned by the leader helper to demonstrate election recovery. This is an explicit destructive fault-injection operation, not an automated correctness test or a safe default diagnostic.
Execs a shell in the pod returned by the leader helper. Validate/quote pod discovery and permissions; an interactive shell is operational access, not a service control API.
Namespace metadata isolates the sample admin’s named resources. It defines no quotas, network policy or permission boundary by itself.
Creates the admin ServiceAccount used by its pod. No RBAC policy appears in this file; existence of an account is not permission hardening.

Admin Deployment exposes fixed UDP 49152, configures Cluster DNS names and mounts 1 GiB memory-backed /dev/shm. Useful fixed egress addressing, but latest-tag images, no readiness/resource limits and no durable state mount remain sample choices.
ClusterIP UDP service maps 49152 to the admin pod. Distinguish advertised/reachable egress address from a local ephemeral socket; session routing must match the actual pod/service topology.
Namespace metadata groups the three Cluster pods under a stable sample name. It supplies namespacing only, without retention, security, scheduling or failure-domain guarantees.
ServiceAccount selected by the Cluster StatefulSet. No RBAC/credential workflow is implemented here; do not infer authenticated application users or Archive authorization.

Three-pod parallel StatefulSet derives node.id from POD_NAME, supplies stable peer DNS names and mounts memory-backed /dev/shm. Stable pod identities help membership, but no persistent Archive/Cluster volumes, anti-affinity or readiness probes are declared; pod replacement can discard its local log.
Headless service provides stable per-pod discovery for the StatefulSet. This is peer naming rather than load balancing; advertised UDP endpoints and DNS startup/readiness still need validation.

Documents applying manifests, execing admin and historical local Minikube/Docker Desktop resource/version settings. These are illustrative manual operations, not tested production sizing or durability/failover acceptance.

Checks tools/Minikube status, builds images, deletes namespaces, loads images and reapplies manifests. No robust fail-fast/deployment rollback; namespace replacement may destroy local state and current root Gradle paths require correction.

Depends on sbe-protocol generated codecs and Agrona; tests open internal-misc. This separation keeps schema generation in one module and behavior demonstrations in another; use Spine existing protocol module instead of duplicate generation.

Console logging uses LOG_LEVEL defaultinfo and time/thread/message pattern; Logback debug=false. Per-message logging and argument boxing/formatting are not a zero-allocation or latency baseline; keep operational logs out of measured hot-path claims.

Seven tests cover header/body wrapping with received blockLength/version, headerless decoding under fixed external layout, repeating groups then trailing varData, corruption from reversed varData writes, precedence-check rejection, correct order and nullString becoming emptyString. Fixed primitives allow offset access, but groups/varData must follow generated cursor order. Decoder String access allocates; tests allocate buffers/flyweights and do not show whole-message zero allocation. Validate schema/bounds before wrapping untrusted bytes; null/empty distinction needs an explicit application encoding.
Test console logger uses LOG_LEVEL defaultinfo with time/thread/message pattern and debug=false; logging configuration is observability boilerplate, not protocol/replay coverage.

Runs two SbeTool tasks into the same generated directory, enables sbe.generate.precedence.checks for the second, then depends on both before compile. Shared declared output ownership can impede caching/parallel safety; use distinct generated directories or one explicit owner when adapting. The second task name is literally generateCodecsWithPrecedeceChecks; tool version1.39.0 differs from Spine1.38.1.

Console logging uses LOG_LEVEL defaultinfo and time/thread/message pattern; Logback debug=false. Per-message logging and argument boxing/formatting are not a zero-allocation or latency baseline; keep operational logs out of measured hot-path claims.

Little-endian schema688/version1 defines SampleSimple(sequence,enum,varData), SampleCorruption(two sequences then data1/data2) and SampleGroup(timestamp, repeated fixed fields+varData, trailing message). UTF-8 length max is1GiB, far above Spine64KiB limit; enforce application limits independently. Unused composite is illustrative type declaration, not a required payload abstraction.

Separate schema689/template1002 repeats the two-fixed/two-varData corruption layout for codecs generated with precedence checks. Keep checked and unchecked schemas/classes distinguishable, and test the runtime check property rather than assuming generation alone enforces access order.

FIX SBE1.0 Draft XSD validates schema/type names, primitive types, presence/version/offset attributes and fixed-field then group then varData structure. The three assigned copies are byte-identical (SHA256 a3dcc0e332f1e8ba348c196454637c524aaef0d9b4d45dfdfe0fe63ff9b0fc44); read once and verify all copies. XSD validation does not validate runtime frame lengths, expected identity, application64KiB limits or logical semantics.
Registers individual cookbook modules and application subprojects.
Builds explanatory local Java examples with Agrona/logging/testing dependencies. No Cluster/Archive dependency or network/durability acceptance exists in this module.

Immutable wrapper stores a logical messageTime and String, allocating per queued message. Logical time expresses causality, not UTC receipt or measured latency; it does not replace Spine capture-clock provenance.

Uses an explicit in-memory message queue and routes to demonstrate send increment and receive max(local,remote)+1. Manual processNextMessage assumes a nonempty queue, and long overflow is unchecked. JDK maps/queue plus newMessage objects are explanatory, not a transport/zero-allocation implementation or total order.

Manually polls three processes in a chosen order to illustrate causally related and independent events. Use it for logical-clock reasoning; selected polling order is not distributed consensus, real scheduling or performance evidence.
Mutable int value command used by the toy reducer. Define immutable/wire command ownership and arithmetic overflow semantics before persisting such commands.

Logs a NewValueEvent current value. Observer notification is not durable output or a checkpoint; keep effects outside replayed deterministic state transitions unless the framework makes them recoverable.
Mutable int multiplier command illustrates deterministic arithmetic input. Pin overflow behavior and canonical encoding if replay equivalence matters.

Mutable int projection event is newly allocated for each notification and shared with listeners. Do not let listeners mutate a shared event, and distinguish state/event value from a committed recorded-output cursor.

Invokes set5, add7, multiply6 sequentially, yielding72 through one local state machine/listener. This is an arithmetic reducer demonstration, with no network replication, committed log or snapshot restore.
Mutable int assignment command illustrates state replacement. Real admission requires validated encoding, stable identity and ordering rather than passing mutable command objects between owners.

Applies set/add/multiply and notifies an ordered listener list with a new event each time. snapshot only notifies listeners; it does not serialize or restore state. The list and synchronous callbacks explain a reducer, not a replicated or durable state machine.
Empty marker command passed to snapshot, which merely emits the current value. Do not treat the class name as a persisted snapshot contract.

Console logging uses LOG_LEVEL defaultinfo and time/thread/message pattern; Logback debug=false. Per-message logging and argument boxing/formatting are not a zero-allocation or latency baseline; keep operational logs out of measured hot-path claims.

Tutorial links deterministic reducer, Cluster-provided time, IPC-local components, UDP endpoint allocation, client egress/keepalives, leader failover and snapshots; command output/JDK guidance may be historical.

Builds C publishers/subscribers, MDS, ping/pong, response-channel samples and diagnostics against shared or static Aeron C client. Raw UDP comparison is Linux-only and links HDR Histogram; cping also links HDR. Release flags add DISABLE_BOUNDS_CHECKS. Install list omits basic_mds_subscriber and raw/ping_pong_raw; source inventory is broader than installed programs. Do not assume release bounds checking or every source being an installed target.

Maps the driver CnC file with a startup timeout, enumerates counter values/labels, prints version/PID/heartbeat age, and supports watch or one-shot mode. Useful for local transport/driver diagnosis; counter values are sampled independently, not an atomic application fence, and human formatting/terminal refresh is outside measured hot paths. Validate update/timeout ranges and monitor registration lifecycles when using counters programmatically.

Creates a manual-control UDP subscription then asynchronously adds the user destination and polls that operation to completion. Uses FragmentAssembler and work-count-aware sleeping polling like basic_subscriber. This demonstrates destination-management control separately from data; add/remove identity, deadlines and logical continuity still need an application contract. Registration/destination waits here are unbounded.

Initializes context/client, starts its conductor, polls asynchronous publication registration and offers stack-built text once per1s. Classifies backpressure/not-connected/admin-action/closed statuses, but advances the loop after failure instead of retrying the same message. MTU-fill helper uses a fixed8192-byte array without checking publication maxPayloadLength against that array; clamp/check actual capacity and snprintf lengths. Successful normal path never changes initial EXIT_FAILURE. This is a diagnostic connectivity demo, not reliable delivery or zero-allocation proof.

Polls async subscription registration, installs available/unavailable image callbacks, and wraps polling in aeron_fragment_assembler_handler before printing complete text. Passes fragments_read into a1ms sleeping strategy and checks negative poll errors. Reuse the complete-message/borrowed-pointer/lifecycle pattern, with bounded startup, exact schema/length validation and logical cursors for Spine; printing assembled text supplies no recovery state.

Pins the first pong Image, owns/release its reference, uses image-level FragmentAssembler, warms the path, resets HDR Histogram and measures one outstanding ping/pong at a time. Stores sender aeron_nano_clock timestamp in the message and subtracts it at the same sender after echo, avoiding cross-host-clock subtraction. Timestamp is refreshed on every offer retry, so RTT excludes preceding retry/admission time. Validate >=8-byte payload/echo length, check histogram range failures and add interruption/deadlines inside retry/receive loops; selected image0 and indefinite waits are demo assumptions.

Owns a ping image and image fragment assembler, then echoes complete borrowed message bytes through an exclusive pong publication. Buffer is consumed synchronously inside callback, with no retained payload copy. Callback spins on every failed offer without terminal-status/interrupt checks, so disconnection can stall the consumer and shutdown. For robust service behavior retain bounded pending output or use an explicitly controlled retry contract; this is transport echo, not committed admission.

Reads CnC metadata to print PID/start/heartbeat or requests driver termination with -T. Default path/timeout and PID-only mode aid diagnosing the exact driver instance. -T is a state-changing administrative action, not a read-only probe; choose the known directory and only invoke termination within explicit owner authorization. A termination request return does not prove graceful Archive/application shutdown.

Reads aggregated distinct errors either from CnC or an explicitly mapped readonly file plus offset, displaying first/last timestamps and observation counts. This preserves repeated-error evidence rather than per-message logging. File offset is parsed but not checked against mapped length before pointer addition/subtraction; enforce bounds before inspecting arbitrary artifacts. Zero listed errors alone does not establish correct delivery/recovery.

Reads the driver loss report via CnC and prints observation counts, lost bytes, session/stream/channel/source plus first/last timestamps. Distinguish observed transport loss from unrecovered logical events; retransmission can repair transport loss while slow consumers still require Archive recovery. The sample is diagnostic output, with no retention/application continuity check.

Assembles fragments before the rate_reporter callback, so payload totals represent complete application messages rather than individual Aeron fragments. Configurable fragment limit and busy-spin polling show throughput-oriented duty cycles. Reporter thread must be halted even on a polling error; this source jumps to cleanup on error after start without halting it. Rate is transport reception, not durable application progress or allocation evidence.

Linux raw-UDP baseline compares connected/unconnected sendto, sendmsg/sendmmsg and recvmsg/recvfrom/recvmmsg using nonblocking sockets; mmsg calls batch only one datagram here. Uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC round-trip timing, warmup/reset and HDR output on fixed32-byte requests, with no Aeron reliability/flow control/framing. Source caveats: -p/-P are advertised/parsed but not handled, receive-type help order differs from implementation, parse return is ignored, invalid inet_pton return0 is not rejected, waits have no timeout and sockets/histogram are not cleaned up. Validate exact configuration and echoed identity before treating it as a trustworthy comparison.

Creates control-mode=response subscription first, gets its registration_id, and appends response-correlation-id to the request publication URI. Reuses the subscription and FragmentAssembler while polling replies through do_work; response routing avoids manual per-client UDP return endpoints. Main sends once then sleeps/polls, does not correlate/durably retry individual application requests, and returns initial EXIT_FAILURE on normal completion. Allocation/URI formatting and startup waits are demo code; check create allocation/partial-failure cleanup and bounded ownership before reuse.

Allocates per-image response state, maps full image correlation_id to that state in an int64-to-pointer map, and protects conductor callback insertion/removal plus application iteration with a mutex. Creates control-mode=response publication per image and waits asynchronously before image-level assembled polling. It holds the mutex through fragment callbacks and sends each reply once; failure can drop replies and stall ownership transitions. snprintf return may exceed the256-byte response array when input is long, so cap/check the offered length. Teardown/partial failures must free every per-image owner, not just delete the map. Correlation routes transport; it does not provide producer deduplication or canonical identity.

Prints image channel/session/MTU/term/source identity; samples counter totals with acquire loads and elapsed aeron_nano_clock intervals, then runs a sleeping1s reporter agent. Reports payload messages/bytes, not wire overhead, recorder acknowledgement or application latency. Lifecycle helpers start/stop the reporter, but callers must stop a started reporter on every failure path before its stack-owned state is released.

Defines image callbacks and an aligned/padded rate_reporter struct with release stores for byte/message totals and a separate reporter agent. The increments are load-plus-store, not atomic fetch-add, so each reporter requires a single update owner; padding reduces sharing but does not make compound updates multi-writer safe. Poll handler counts callbacks; place it behind assembly when measuring complete messages.

Centralizes demo UDP endpoints/streams,32-byte messages,10-million measured/100000 warmup messages, fragment limit10 and zero linger. Also defines response-control/request channel defaults. These are constants for wiring and synthetic load, not real-feed limits, discovery, durability or performance budgets; externalize isolated ports before running concurrent fixtures.

Uses one exclusive publication and reusable aeron_buffer_claim_t, writes the sequence directly into claim.data then commits, avoiding the offer payload copy for an unfragmented message. Validate length>=8 and <=maxPayloadLength, and abort a claim on encoding failure. Concrete pinned-source bug: -L parses into messages rather than message_length; printed totals also use requested count and error exit can still become success. Other negative claim statuses are treated as backpressure. Correct those before benchmarking;64KiB Spine frames generally require offer/fragmentation, not a tiny-MTU claim.

Allocates/zeros one reusable payload, writes sequence at its start and repeatedly offers it using busy spin, with optional linger and a separate rate reporter. It retries every negative status as backpressure, lacks a minimum8-byte length check before writing uint64, and after interruption can count a message that was never successfully offered. Printed aggregate totals use requested messages, not message_sent_count. Classify terminal statuses, count only successful offers and bound retries before using its rates as acceptance evidence.

Uses asynchronous add/find publication, shared_ptr ownership, aligned fixed256-byte payload plus AtomicBuffer and exact formatted length; classifies offer status and sends every1s. Failed offers still advance the application loop and readiness wait ignores timeout/interrupt. Take buffer reuse/status distinctions, but retain exact pending bytes and advance only on actual acceptance; formatting/std::cout are not allocation-free hot-path evidence.

Uses RAII client/subscription ownership, registration/image callbacks, FragmentAssembler and work-count-aware SleepingIdleStrategy. Callback honors offset/length but constructs std::string and prints each assembled message. Keep borrowed-view lifetime and complete-frame handling; add schema/bounds/logical cursor checks and bounded startup for application use.

Builds the named C++ samples against aeron_client_wrapper plus shared/static C client, with HDR dependencies for ping programs and release DISABLE_BOUNDS_CHECKS. ExclusiveThroughput.cpp exists but is not an add_executable target in this file; do not claim it is compiled by the sample build. StreamingPublisher is built but omitted from the install list. Preserve bounds checks during validation and inspect exact wrapper/backend API versions before adopting code.

Provides namespaced C++ demo channel/stream/warmup/count/length/linger/fragment-limit constants matching the small synthetic transport profile. std::string constants and command-line ownership are startup allocations; constants are not production connection discovery, a64KiB framing policy or a performance envelope.

Same one-process threaded ping/pong profile as PingPong, but both outputs use ExclusivePublication owned by their respective application threads. It still uses offer, not tryClaim; exclusivity is not proof of zero-copy payload emission. Assembled echo, pretouch and HDR warmup are useful, while image0/position symmetry, ABI-specific time_point bytes, timestamp refresh and unbounded inner retries remain demo constraints.

Source-only variant uses ExclusivePublication claims and pins receiver image0, also reporting empty/nonempty poll ratios. It is not a target of the accompanying CMake file. Plain failedPolls/successfulPolls are written by poll thread and read before join without synchronization, and an interrupted unsuccessful claim loop can fall through to writing/committing an unclaimed BufferClaim. Correct those concrete defects and establish a final application fence before using any output; no measured throughput or correctness claim is made for this file.

Exclusive ping publication plus pong image0, preTouchMappedMemory, warmup, FragmentAssembler and HDR Histogram demonstrate serialized RTT measurement. Sender steady_clock::time_point bytes are echoed and subtracted at the same process, so this is round trip rather than one-way synchronization. Encoding time_point object bytes is ABI-specific; define a numeric wire timestamp and check enough bytes. Timestamp refresh excludes offer retry delay; comparing separate ping/pong physical positions assumes matching geometry. Interrupt checks exist, but deadlines, histogram validation/cleanup and exact response correlation remain necessary.

Runs ping and pong in one process on separate application threads using ordinary publications, first-image polling, pretouched mapped memory, assembled echo, warmup/reset and HDR RTT/RTTs-per-second output. OnScopeExit stops/joins pong thread. Sender timestamp is refreshed before each offer attempt, and physical position comparison assumes symmetric recording geometry; inner wait/offer loops ignore running/deadlines and may hang. Report this topology/serialized workload explicitly rather than generalizing its result to separate-process admission, Archive or live-feed performance.

Echoes assembled borrowed ping bytes through an exclusive pong publication with a success fast path, then busy-spin retries. Optional pretouch shifts initial page-fault work toward startup; it does not eliminate all allocation/cold behavior. Callback retry lacks interruption/terminal-status bounds; it can prevent subscription progress and shutdown when pong transport closes. This is an echo responder, not reliable recorded output.

Padded std::atomic byte/message totals are release-stored by onMessage and acquire-read on a reporter thread, with steady_clock elapsed-rate calculation and configurable sleep interval. onMessage uses separate load/store increments, so require one updating thread; totals are not an atomic pair. reset/report mutate plain baseline fields and require owner serialization. This measures payload reception/offering rates, not wire bytes, complete recorded fences or immutable application state.

Assembles messages before RateReporter counting, polls with BusySpinIdleStrategy and uses OnScopeExit to halt/join reporter thread before its captured state dies. Configurable fragment limit affects duty-cycle latency/throughput. Receiver rates do not prove sequence/digest/state preservation; report actual complete applied/recorded counts for Spine and account for busy-spin CPU.

Allocates one payload array, writes a sequence, optionally chooses random lengths>=8, and offers with a reset busy-spin strategy. Optional progress thread is halted/joined through scope cleanup; no-progress mode resets/reports rates synchronously. Any negative offer is counted as backpressure, interruption inside retry can still count an unsent message, and requested-count denominator misstates shortened runs. Random source is seeded from random_device, so record a deterministic seed/distribution if reproducibility is required.

Starts concurrent poll and optional reporter threads, validates messageLength<=maxPayloadLength, repeatedly tryClaims into a reusable BufferClaim, writes sequence at claim.offset and commits. FragmentAssembler and receiver-side RateReporter count complete received messages; scope exit joins threads. Claim retries treat all negatives alike and omit interruption checks inside the inner loop; after send completion it reports without waiting for a final consumer fence. It demonstrates unfragmented transport throughput, not all requested messages applied/durable, and cannot claim arbitrary64KiB frames at default MTU.

Read latest valid CM snapshot and compute per-service next/log session bounds from pending messages; rewrite a temporary recording, require equal stop positions, truncate old snapshot and replicate replacement. Preserves ordinary session/timer records while renumbering pending service headers. Take backups, stop CM/services and keep framework-version compatibility explicit before invoking destructive repair.

Agent creates response subscription first, then an exclusive request publication carrying its registration ID as responseCorrelationId; polls reply fragments and exposes nonblocking offer. revokeOnClose removes response linkage. Call close only after doWork has initialized resources, or add null-safe cleanup.

Image lifecycle callbacks feed bounded OneToOneConcurrentArrayQueues; agent maps Image.correlationId to response publications and per-client handlers using Long2ObjectHashMap. ControlledFragmentAssembler ABORTs unprocessed requests and frees session builders on Image removal. Optional prototype publication pre-allocates response transport; borrowed Aeron ownership is preserved.

Reads CnC version/PID/heartbeat and filters counter keys by type, registration identity, session, stream and channel regex. The watch loop is operational display code; route the correct aeron.dir and close a long-lived mapping when embedding it.

Groups stream counters by session/stream/channel and calculates publisher remaining window, publisher-to-sender backlog and receiver-HWM-to-subscriber backlog. Useful attribution formulas; the gathered values are not a coherent simultaneous snapshot.

Optional embedded-driver directory wiring and scoped publication ownership. It offers one numbered ASCII message per second and prints negative results instead of resending; the numbered loop is not reliable admission.

Optional embedded-driver shutdown hooks plus available/unavailable Image callbacks. It delegates complete-message polling to SamplesUtil, which installs FragmentAssembler. Printing within handlers changes latency.

Read-only CnC mapping with version validation, CountersReader, driver PID and volatile ring-buffer heartbeat access; AutoCloseable releases the map. Local process diagnostics require the matching CnC file and version.

Read-only PID/version/start/activity display, or writable to-driver ManyToOneRingBuffer plus DriverProxy termination request. The terminate mode changes runtime state and requires an intentional operational action.

Concurrent publication tryClaim loop with one reusable BufferClaim, field write into claim.buffer()/offset(), then commit. Only a small example field is populated; enforce payload bounds and abort partially encoded claims.

Two manual MDC publications, different control endpoints/tags, explicitly add the same destination and await two Images. The loop alternates attempts instead of blocking one source behind the other. MDC is multiple unicast deliveries, not native IP multicast.

Same direct term-buffer encoding pattern using an exclusive publication. It is the closest simple SBE claim-loop example, but does not validate all terminal states or supply encoding-exception cleanup.
Exclusive variant of the same IPC topology. The aligned DirectBuffer and idle strategy are created once in the publisher thread; cached publication/running locals keep the inner loop small.

UDP publication plus local aeron-spy subscription, with spiesSimulateConnection(true), reads publication term buffers without network receive. This is useful for a local critical recorder with remote UDP fanout; spy connection/flow-control effects must be intentional.

Same baseline shape with ExclusivePublication. Compare against EmbeddedThroughput under identical channel/load/driver settings to isolate publisher arbitration rather than attributing all improvement to exclusivity.

Two UnsafeBuffer views and a reusable DirectBufferVector array combine a 16-byte prefix with the remaining body. Validate configured messageLength is at least 16; the vectors are reused, not allocated per offer.

Same-host IPC with SHARED driver, separate publisher/subscriber/reporter threads and a direct buffer allocated once to publication.maxMessageLength(). Stop flag is checked inside backpressure loops; a successful offer remains transport-only evidence.

Same-process ping/pong with DEDICATED driver, no-op sender/receiver idle strategies and short conductor backoff. Pong preserves fragment flags when tryClaim-copying each incoming fragment. The send-position wait assumes the mirrored transport layout; prefer application correlation for general protocols.

Baseline concurrent publication, subscriber executor, shared rate reporter and reused direct buffer on a configurable channel. It retries all negative offers and uses an interactive repeat barrier; useful comparative transport load, not a service recovery test.

Reads Agrona’s distinct error log from CnC or an explicit file/offset and prints counts plus first/last timestamps. It unmaps in finally; use this before concluding a poll timeout was ordinary backpressure.

FragmentAssembler dispatches create/chunk message types; Long2ObjectHashMap associates transfer correlation IDs with mapped files, then unmaps on last chunk. Add filename/path, length, offset, missing-session and integrity validation before production reuse; mapping/unmapping alone is not a durability protocol.

Read-only mapped input file; a correlation/version/type header precedes maxPayloadLength-sized chunks encoded directly via a reusable BufferClaim. It checks terminal offer codes. Claim writes need abort on encoding failure; there is no receiver completion acknowledgement.

Read subscriber totals once per second and estimate message count from configured fixed message length. Wall-clock elapsed time and fixed-size inference make it unsuitable for variable-size latency or exact admission accounting.

Pin one Image after connect and use ImageFragmentAssembler, lazy-set byte totals and failed/successful poll counts. It does not reacquire an Image after publisher rollover; use lifecycle-aware consumption for reconnects.

Read-only LogBuffers traversal exposes metadata/raw tails and aligned DATA frames, optionally scanning zero gaps. Hex is lossless byte display; ASCII replaces negative bytes with NUL. This diagnoses transport bytes, not a canonical-envelope validator.

Strict named-option parsing for hex/ascii output, default-header omission and zero scanning, then delegates LogInspector.run. This wrapper rejects unknown/invalid options, while the underlying formatter defaults unknown formats to hex.
Maps the local loss-report file and emits CSV via LossReportReader. Absence of that file and zero entries are different observations; loss diagnostics do not prove end-to-end application continuity.

Loads property files, disables sparse terms, enables the Windows high-resolution timer and runs DEDICATED agents with busy-spin conductor/no-op sender/receiver. This is an aggressive CPU policy, not a universally optimal deployment default.

Two publications share an endpoint but use different stream IDs; 10,000/9,000-byte payloads exercise Aeron fragmentation. Each publication advances only on successful offer. Console-heavy spinning and unspecified terminal-result handling are demo shortcuts.

Separate FragmentAssembler instances isolate the two streams and validate reconstructed lengths. Image handlers expose source/session lifecycle. Prefer idle(totalWork) over copying its accumulating idleCount argument pattern.

Reusable aligned buffer, sender nanoTime timestamp, single in-flight ping, ImageFragmentAssembler, warmup iterations and RTT histogram. The timestamp is rewritten on each failed offer, so the measurement omits offer waiting; no deadline bounds lost-response waits.

Pins the first Image and echoes the borrowed complete-message buffer through publication.offer. Busy-spin retry occurs inside the input callback; suitable for a microbenchmark, but can prevent useful work if output is permanently blocked.

Cache-line padding and volatile long fields published through AtomicLongFieldUpdater.lazySet separate the data path from a parked reporting thread. Updates assume a single writer; multiplying by reportIntervalNs means its advertised per-second units require a one-second interval.

Separates subscription polling from rate reporting with an optional embedded driver. RateReporter uses an independent running flag; shutdown code does not halt that reporter explicitly, so do not copy this lifecycle unchanged.

System-property controlled channels, stream IDs, message/fragment counts, warmup, linger, exclusivity and idle strategy. Defaults include 32-byte payload, fragment limit 10 and BusySpinIdleStrategy; freeze these settings with any result rather than inheriting mutable defaults.

Subscriber-loop helper constructs one FragmentAssembler, idles with actual work count, exposes Image identity and maps local CnC counters. findLatestRecording uses channel-fragment/stream matching; it is not an exact logical-log identity or cross-generation continuity catalog.

Finds the driver’s controllable idle status indicator and changes it with a release write. This is a runtime tuning tool only when that strategy is configured, not a generic replacement for per-agent idle suppliers.

Minimal aligned direct UnsafeBuffer, external driver connection, one UDP publication and a five-second connection deadline. Its single failed offer is only printed; use explicit retry/failure semantics for a reliable producer.

Poll a subscription with BackoffIdleStrategy and a bounded fragment count. The handler allocates a byte array/string and exits after one fragment; it is introductory code, not fragmented-message decoding or a low-allocation consumer.

Groups and sorts per-stream position/BPE/NAK counters; recovers fuller channel text from labels when keys truncate URI data. TreeMap is deliberate ordered presentation; primitive/object Agrona maps cache auxiliary channel state.

Reuse one aligned buffer, embed a sequence, reset the idle strategy per retry and count backpressure. Random lengths exercise payload sizes. The loop retries every negative result forever and measures offered throughput, not durable/apply latency.

Migration fixture generator creates one recording at position zero and another starting in a later term, with small terms/segments. It waits recorder completion before stop but deletes Archive contents on startup and uses fileSyncLevel(0); never run against valuable data.

Exclusive publication recorded locally with spiesSimulateConnection(true); reuse direct buffer and wait recorder position before reporting. Repeated runs truncate earlier recording after DELETE signal. No sync/lifecycle/deadline checks in the hot wait make it a recording benchmark, not durable storage acceptance.

Create an exact session-specific recording, verify recorder completion, replay a fixed length and validate embedded message count with ImageFragmentAssembler. The reported throughput includes replay connection setup; interrupted/closed replay prints a warning rather than proving full-range completion.

Primary local spy and secondary tagged replication run the same indexer over source bytes; compare sequence, timestamps and physical positions. Agrona LongArrayList stores indexes, with 126 positions batched into 1 KiB index messages. Index state commits only after batch publication succeeds via controlled ABORT; arrays are unbounded and the final partial batch is not flushed as a persisted index.

PersistentSubscription combines replay-on-start/reconnect with live consumption using separate replay stream and lifecycle listener. Default replay endpoint localhost:0 is resolved by the library. One latest recording and printed output do not implement output-generation rollover or application checkpoint atomicity.

Starts a LOCAL recording, locates its local RecordingPos by publication session and archiveId, then waits for the final publication position before stop. It checks asynchronous Archive errors. Single-shot message offers are printed rather than retried, so missing messages remain possible.

Mutable pooled descriptor carries all Archive catalog fields; retain() prevents collector reuse. Borrowed descriptors otherwise change at reset, so copy/retain before storing them as identity evidence.

Reuse a bounded descriptor pool while building each list response; reset releases unretained objects. Pool size limits retained reusable objects, not every response or total list size; callers still choose pagination and retained ownership.

Destination Archive pulls from a source control endpoint and waits SYNC then REPLICATE_END. Existing destination replacement first truncates to start and waits DELETE; this is destructive migration, not an automatic append/repair policy.

Matches asynchronous signals by correlation or recording ID, preserving IDs/positions absent from later signal fields. Distinguishes unexpected REPLICATE_END while awaiting SYNC. Single latest-signal storage and unbounded waits assume serial operations; add bounded deadlines for operational use.

Manual multi-destination subscription plus ReplayMerge adds replay/live destinations for the same recorded session, then switches to live. It wraps FragmentAssembler and surfaces merge failure. Fixed localhost endpoints and one-shot latest-recording selection require deployment-specific replacement.

Find a recording, start an effectively unbounded replay on a distinct stream, then subscribe to the replay’s actual session ID. Its first-100-recordings/latest-channel choice and raw fragment printing are shortcuts; a logical range needs exact identity, pagination and complete-message handling.

Demonstrates connect/challenge/authenticate/reject transitions with a primitive session map and hardcoded ASCII credentials. Authenticate results must be retried until accepted. Challenge-path principal handling differs from the no-challenge path; this is not a secure credential service.
Creates a fresh SampleAuthenticator for each configured authenticator instance, avoiding accidentally sharing its mutable session state across agents.
Agrona ObjectHashSet allowlist accepts a principal string but ignores protocol/action/resource type. Appropriate to demonstrate the hook; least-privilege Archive policies need action-aware checks.
Shared MB conversion, no-op fragment callback and temporary Archive directory helper. Temporary directory creation and cleanup support demos; there is no runtime persistence abstraction to copy.

Read-only mapped .rec segment traversal advances by 32-byte frame alignment, exposes header flyweight and optional payload dump. Stops on a short/unwritten frame; it does not establish complete canonical messages or repair a truncated recording.
Archive sample package documentation; no runtime behavior.

Builds node-specific ports/directories, public/internal hosts, local IPC Archive context, UDP control/replication endpoints and one or multiple service containers. Service IDs are explicit. NoOpLock only fits confined clients; do not extrapolate localhost/topology defaults to multicast or HA ownership.

Capture Cluster and its idle strategy, then retry session egress only three times. State/snapshots are empty and remaining failures drop the response; this precisely demonstrates why transient egress cannot be the canonical recovery source.

Loads member/host lists, builds ClusterConfig, wires component-specific error handlers and shared termination barrier, then launches ClusteredMediaDriver plus service container. Printed errors are diagnostic, not a fail-closed policy for arbitrary application invariants.
Cluster sample package marker; no runtime behavior.

Reusable bid buffer and EgressListener for replies/session/leader changes; pollEgress during ingress retries and send keepalives while idle. Random bid timing is external to the service. Successful ingress offer is not admission acknowledgement; client has no durable retry/dedup spool.

Deterministic integer-price auction state, correlation-bearing reply, snapshot store/load and null-session egress guard. Snapshot validation uses Java asserts and only one small frame; production needs explicit complete/exact framing and callback failure handling.

Static three-node port scheme, separate Archive/client/member/log/catchup endpoints, local IPC Archive access, min multicast flow-control supplier and UDP replication. The supplier choice does not make every channel native multicast; endpoints and network capability determine transport.

Embedded lifecycle fixture demonstrates clean/recover startup, snapshot control toggle/count and Cluster timers with service-prefixed correlation ID. Service assumes non-null session, restores one unchecked snapshot frame and offers best-effort echo; single node proves local recovery, not quorum HA.
Tutorial package documentation marker for source snippets; no runtime behavior.
Immutable correlation ID and subscription/publication channel/stream parameters carried through the provisioning queue; inherited completion supplies acknowledgement.

ControlledFragmentHandler offers the borrowed fragment and ABORTs on NOT_CONNECTED/BACK_PRESSURED/ADMIN_ACTION, counting successful fragments/bytes only after success. CLOSED/MAX_POSITION_EXCEEDED return CONTINUE and drop input; Spine must fail/latch those terminal results.

ManyToOneConcurrentArrayQueue(1024) transfers management commands into an agent-owned Long2ObjectHashMap of EchoPairs. Resource/MBean setup rolls back on failure. Blocking await has no deadline, and queue.add can reject full queues; handle both explicitly.

Connects to a fixed localhost JMX endpoint, creates one EchoPair and reads its backpressure monitor. Credentials/transport security, connection cleanup and arbitrary deployment endpoint resolution are omitted.

Mutex wait-loop plus complete/notifyAll communicates a command result or exception back to its caller. It is a synchronous control-plane acknowledgement, not a durable message or data-plane primitive.

AgentRunner owns Provisioning work, registers its MBean onStart, chooses external or embedded driver and closes runner/client/driver. Error printing and quiet close are sample lifecycle choices; establish complete EchoPair cleanup when embedding.
Marker command selecting cleanup of all owned echo resources/MBeans; it shares the completion protocol rather than implementing a separate callback path.
Read-only counters for correlation ID, backpressure, successful fragments and bytes; supporting operational interface, not a recorded progress acknowledgement.
Central MBean naming with correlation-specific EchoPair names; keeps management identity separate from Aeron session IDs.
Management contract for create/remove-all requests; synchronous calls cross into the provisioning agent through its command queue.
Package documentation marker for the executable samples; no runtime behavior.

Send bounded packet bursts then verify exact ordered replies with RTT histogram; varies packet and burst sizes. The receive channel is left blocking by this sample, and loss can stall the run; it is not an offered-load tail-latency harness.
Shared ping/pong ports and destinations; configures nonblocking DatagramChannel and SO_REUSEADDR, with optional connected peer for write(). Supporting socket setup, not a reliability layer.
Poll multiple nonblocking receive sockets and send preserved sequence/timestamp back to configured remote host. Copies the received length into reply; no sender authentication or Aeron framing.
Receive from multiple sockets then reply through a connected write channel. Re-encodes only two longs rather than forwarding arbitrary received payload; pair with its matching fixed-format ping.
Selector-driven echo with IntSupplier attachment and selected-key removal. Callback catches/prints IOException and continues; this is not fail-closed message processing.
Unconnected send(), scan one or more receive channels, verify echoed sequence and record RTT; configurable remote host. It does not retry failed/short sends or repair dropped datagrams.

Attach callback to selector key, send timestamped packet, selectNow-spin and remove each processed key. Contrasts readiness scanning with direct receive polling; shutdown and stalled response are still benchmark-specific.

Connected DatagramChannel.write() variant with multiple receive channels and sequence/RTT checks. Helps isolate connected-send overhead; hardcoded localhost peers and unchecked send progress are benchmark constraints.
Raw UDP package marker; no runtime behavior.

Builder creates credential-to-principal Object2ObjectHashMap and session-to-principal Long2ObjectHashMap; successful authenticate removes session state, unknown credentials reject. Challenge callbacks are unsupported, and credential arrays are retained by reference.

Principal-specific rules precede general rules and fallback default (DENY_ALL); within a principal use type allow/deny sets, BiInt2ObjectMap protocol/action rules and Int2ObjectHashMap protocol rules. Type allow is checked before deny; document that precedence and keep byte-array keys immutable.
Table-driven reflected CRC64 updates byte arrays or DirectBuffer without a payload copy; recalculate resets state and main checks known vectors. One mutable CRC instance is agent confined.
Reusable supplier carries a correlation long into frame reservedValue. Mutable value is safe only under publication-owner confinement; reserved transport metadata is separate from application schema.

Two response subscriptions and Long2LongCounterMap count four expected responses per request from the 2x2 fanout topology. Deterministic payload/MTU sweep exposes fragmentation/MDC issues; exact uniqueness of the four responder identities is not enforced by the count alone.

Two controlled input assemblers feed one dynamic-MDC response publication; validation and send/receive counters advance on successful offer. Agent confines shared CRC/supplier, but terminal failures and wait-for-all-receivers need explicit operational policy.

Random(42) payloads, CRC prefix, exclusive offers and bounded Long2ObjectHashMap of in-flight correlations across message/MTU sweep. Five-second no-response guard uses last send rather than a deadline per request; doWork returns sends despite receiving work.

ControlledFragmentAssembler validates CRC then echoes full messages with reused reserved-value supplier; negative offers ABORT, successful offers COMMIT. Terminal publication results can retry forever, so harden the result policy before copying.

Builders define unicast and dynamic MDC endpoints plus group tags; taggedFlowControl requires two matching receivers and five-second timeout. MTU sweep includes jumbo sizes up to max UDP payload, so treat it as adversarial transport coverage, not a recommended network profile.

Checks invalid paths, no-op valid snapshots and deliberately corrupted pending-service bounds across two services/three nodes. Rewrites leader snapshot, verifies counts/IDs, replicates to followers and restarts before new messages/timers. This is substantive recovery evidence for the repair tool, not permission to silently repair application history.
Parameterized byte boundaries confirm ASCII renders negative signed bytes as NUL, not their hexadecimal value. Use hex when exact binary evidence matters.
Happy-path defaults/options plus unknown, missing and invalid values and positional count rejection. Narrow parseArgs makes CLI validation testable without invoking System.exit.
Hex/ascii aliases, unknown-format fallback, offset/length and zero-length behavior. Confirms inspection presentation semantics, not Aeron frame or application schema validation.

Builds real log-layout fixture with term metadata/default header and body, then captures run output to verify metadata, formats and dump limits. The fixture has one simple frame, not a fragmented/corrupt stream recovery case.

Real driver fixture spans IPC, shared concurrent publication sessions, explicit initial positions, long aliases and truncated channel keys; verifies sorted statistics/full URI reconstruction. Counter polling and expected values are transport diagnostics, not transactional progress.

Real Archive creates recordings, pages catalog and verifies pooled reuse, retain() isolation and zero-pool behavior. Its createRecordings recorder wait comparison is reversed, so do not copy that helper as recording-completion evidence.

Two independent drivers/Archives test empty/nonempty new replication and replacement of an existing differently positioned recording. Waits STOP signal, checks descriptors and honors actual replication channel. Descriptor equality is covered; complete replay byte equality is not asserted here.
Mocks SessionProxy to verify valid/invalid credentials and simultaneous session identities. It does not test challenge handling, mutable-key safety or retries after authenticate returns false.

Parameterized allow/deny defaults, protocol/action/type rules, principal override of general rules and unspecified fallback. Use its precedence scenarios when composing Archive/Cluster authorisation policies.
